name: Keezhaperumpallam Naganathaswamy Temple
deity: Shiva as Naganathaswamy, with the Goddess Vaidhyanayaki; the shrine of Ketu is the principal draw
summary: The Navagraha temple for Ketu, the descending lunar node, near ancient Poompuhar. Shiva is worshipped here as Naganathaswamy with the Goddess Vaidhyanayaki, but devotees come chiefly to the shrine of Ketu.

sections.history: This stone temple grew out of the great age of Chola building, when the Kaveri delta was studded with shrines of cut granite. Its sanctity, however, is older still: Naganathaswamy is sung in the Tevaram, the Tamil hymns of the Nayanmar saints, marking it as one of the Paadal Petra Sthalams. It stands near the ancient port of Poompuhar, once Kaveripoompattinam, where the river meets the sea and where merchants and pilgrims have gathered for centuries. Over generations the temple became fixed in the pilgrim mind as the abode of Ketu, one of the nine Navagraha shrines spread across the delta.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian idiom of the Chola country: a granite sanctum crowned by a vimana, an entrance tower, and pillared halls that open onto the central shrine of Shiva as Naganathaswamy. The Goddess Vaidhyanayaki has her own shrine within the enclosure. What sets the temple apart is the prominence given to Ketu, whose shrine is treated as a destination in its own right; devotees circle it, light lamps, and make offerings there. The layout is compact and functional, shaped less for grandeur than for the steady rhythm of daily worship and the flow of pilgrims moving between the planetary shrines of the region.
sections.legends: The temple's legend reaches back to the churning of the ocean of milk. When the serpent-demon who had slipped among the gods was cut in two, his severed body became Ketu, the shadow planet. According to the sthala tradition, the serpent king worshipped Shiva at this place and received his grace, and through that grace Ketu attained his fixed station among the nine planets. Because of this, the temple is revered as the Ketu Sthalam. Pilgrims pray here for relief from Ketu dosha and naga dosha, for release from hidden and long-standing obstacles, and for spiritual progress leading toward moksha.
sections.festivals: Worship centred on Ketu marks the temple's calendar, and devotees time their visits to the planetary periods believed to be governed by Ketu. Pradosham, the twilight worship of Shiva observed twice each lunar month, draws steady crowds, and annual festivals bring processions and special rituals. Abhishekam, the ceremonial bathing of the deity, and the lighting of lamps before Ketu are the offerings most sought by those seeking relief from doshas.
sections.experience: A visit here is quieter and more purposeful than at the great tourist temples. Most who come are pilgrims working through the nine Navagraha shrines, and the mood at the Ketu sanctum is one of earnest, unhurried prayer. You will see devotees circling the shrine, offering lamps, and sitting in the halls in the hush of the delta afternoon. The nearness of Poompuhar and the sea lends the place an open, coastal light, and the surrounding country of paddy and coconut carries the calm of rural Tamil Nadu.

visit.timings: Open roughly 7:00 am to 12:30 pm and 4:00 to 8:00 pm; timings vary, so verify locally before travelling.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected; cover shoulders and legs, and remove footwear before entering.
visit.photography: Photography inside the sanctum is generally not permitted; ask temple staff before taking any photographs.
visit.gettingThere: Keezhaperumpallam lies near Poompuhar in Mayiladuthurai district, close to the coast, about 25 km from Sirkazhi. The nearest railhead is Sirkazhi, and Mayiladuthurai is a convenient hub; the nearest airport is Tiruchirappalli, about 170 km away.
